evidence_items.claim: Do not present a reconstructed divine-council system as the only possible reading of every plural heavenly-being text.

Ancient background for Dead Sea Scrolls includes inscriptions, material culture, excavation layers, and imperial administration; the entry ties that world to Isaiah 40, Psalm 119, qumran-archaeological-site, and qumran-caves without letting comparison replace the biblical witness.

Historically, Dead Sea Scrolls is located by its canonical setting; this entry connects that setting with qumran-archaeological-site, qumran-caves, isaiah and related CKL objects for contextual retrieval.
The Masoretic, Qumran, and Greek textual traditions differ in the phrase that describes the allocation of the nations in Deuteronomy 32:8.
The variant directly affects whether Deuteronomy 32:8 names Israel or divine beings when describing the nations' boundaries and therefore must precede worldview reconstruction.
Deuteronomy moves from remembered wilderness history through covenant instruction to covenant consequences, renewal, succession, song, blessing, and Moses's death.

Ancient background for Divine Justice includes covenant life, temple worship, royal ideology, wisdom teaching, and early church confession; the entry ties that world to Deuteronomy 32:3-4, Micah 6:6-8, justice-theme, and amos without letting comparison replace the biblical witness.
Divine Justice is read across the canon as Scripture develops this theme from Israel's story into the New Testament witness.
